pillars.name: NVIDIA and the chip supply chain
AI supply chain and market leadership

indicators.name: Capex growth vs revenue growth (gap)
indicators.source: SEC XBRL: MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, ORCL
indicators.rule: Heat 20 at zero gap, 60 at +25 pts, 90 at +50 pts. The AI-bubble question in one number: is spending outrunning the revenue it is meant to earn?
indicators.detail: Hyperscaler capex is $691.0B over the last 12 months (+93% vs a year earlier) while their revenue grew +19%.

indicators.name: Capex as a share of revenue
indicators.rule: Heat = where today sits among the last 33 quarters of the group's own history (100 = highest ever recorded).
indicators.detail: The five spend 36 cents of every revenue dollar on property and equipment, against a low of 10% and a high of 36% in this history.

indicators.name: Capex as a share of operating cash flow
indicators.rule: Heat is the higher of the history percentile and a floor rule (70% = 55, 100% = 90): above 100% means spending exceeds the cash the business makes.
indicators.detail: At 95%, spending on buildout uses 95 of every $100 of operating cash flow. Above 100% requires borrowing, asset sales or cash on hand.

indicators.name: Free cash flow after capex (trend)
indicators.rule: Heat 40 if flat, 75 if down 30%, 95 if down 60%. Falling free cash flow while capex climbs is how bubbles become financing problems.
indicators.detail: Combined free cash flow is $32.7B over 12 months ($201.1B a year earlier).

indicators.name: Capex growth: is it slowing?
indicators.rule: Heat 75 if year-over-year growth slowed 5+ pts in each of the last two quarters (the commonly cited demand-cliff signal), 55 if once, else 20.
indicators.detail: Latest quarter's capex grew +118% year over year versus +87% the quarter before and +91% before that.

indicators.name: Cloud backlog growth vs capex growth
indicators.source: SEC XBRL RemainingPerformanceObligation (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, ORCL)
indicators.rule: Heat 40 when backlog grows as fast as capex, 85 when capex outgrows contracted backlog by 40 pts. Backlog is customers' signed commitments, the hardest evidence of real demand.
indicators.detail: Signed-but-not-yet-delivered revenue at MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, ORCL totals $1.96T, +89% over a year; capex is +93%.

indicators.name: NVIDIA revenue growth (is it decelerating?)
indicators.display: +106% year over year, +18% on the quarter
indicators.rule: Heat is set by the change in year-over-year growth versus last quarter: -30 pts = 90, -10 = 65, flat = 35, +15 = 15. NVIDIA's revenue is the clearest read on AI hardware demand.
indicators.detail: Quarterly revenue is $96.2B (+106%). Growth moved +21 pts from last quarter's +85%.

indicators.name: NVIDIA receivable days (how long customers take to pay)
indicators.rule: Heat is the higher of the history percentile and a jump rule (+8 days in a quarter = 55, +20 = 90). Rising receivable days can mean customers are stretching, or that sales are being financed.
indicators.detail: Customers owe NVIDIA $63.1B, equal to 60 days of sales. It was 45 days a quarter ago and 32 at the quietest point on record.

indicators.name: NVIDIA inventory days
indicators.rule: Heat = history percentile (100 = most inventory relative to sales in the record). Inventory building faster than sales is an early sign of demand cooling or over-ordering.
indicators.detail: Unsold chips and parts equal 119 days of sales, versus a range of 41 to 212 days over the record.

indicators.name: NVIDIA supply commitments vs sales
indicators.rule: Heat = history percentile of purchase commitments relative to the last year's sales. Big commitments to suppliers are a bet that demand keeps growing.
indicators.detail: NVIDIA has committed $45.8B to suppliers (about 15% of its last four quarters' revenue).

indicators.name: NVIDIA borrowing
indicators.rule: Heat 15 if flat, 50 if debt rose $5B in a quarter, 85 if $20B. NVIDIA has long been net cash; new borrowing by the main supplier is notable, because it can mean funding customers or buybacks beyond cash flow.
indicators.detail: Long-term debt moved from $7.5B to $32.4B.

indicators.name: AI chip peers' revenue growth (AMD, Broadcom, Micron)
indicators.rule: A U-shape: heat is high if peers' growth has stalled (the buildout is slowing) and rises again if it is extreme (an overheated cycle). 15-40% growth is the calm middle.
indicators.detail: Latest-quarter revenue growth over a year earlier for the other AI-exposed chip makers.

indicators.name: NVIDIA's weight in the US stock market
indicators.display: 5.2% of the combined value of US-listed stocks we track
indicators.rule: Heat 35 at 3%, 65 at 5%, 92 at 8%. When one company carries this much of the index, its fortunes become the market's.
indicators.detail: NVIDIA is 5.2% of $99.3T of total market value in our universe.

indicators.name: NVIDIA share price: stretch above its 200-day average
indicators.display: +0% above its 200-day average; -1% over 3 months; volatility 32%
indicators.rule: Heat = where today's stretch ranks among the last 1055 days of NVIDIA's own history.
indicators.detail: How far the bellwether is running ahead of its trend.

indicators.name: NVIDIA insider selling
indicators.display: $968M sold in 90 days (3.2x the usual pace); $0.0M bought
indicators.rule: Heat 30 at the usual pace, 60 at double, 90 at four times. Insiders sell for many reasons (taxes, scheduled plans), so this is weak evidence alone.
indicators.detail: Insiders' sales over the last 90 days versus their average over the three 90-day periods before.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler long-term debt growth
indicators.source: SEC XBRL (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, ORCL)
indicators.rule: Heat 15 flat, 55 at +25%, 90 at +60%. Companies that used to fund buildout from cash are increasingly borrowing.
indicators.detail: Total long-term debt for the group versus a year earlier.

indicators.name: Bank loans to non-bank lenders (the private-credit pipeline)
indicators.display: $2119B, +20.3% over a year (+21% annualized over 13 weeks)
indicators.rule: Heat = where the year-over-year growth ranks since 2009. Banks lending to private-credit funds, REITs and other lenders is a main channel through which GPU and data-center financing reaches the economy.
indicators.detail: Loans from US commercial banks to non-depository financial institutions.

indicators.name: Bank commercial and industrial loans
indicators.rule: Heat = history percentile since 2009 of yearly growth.
indicators.detail: Business borrowing from banks, a broad measure of how freely credit is flowing.

indicators.name: Banks tightening loan standards (large firms)
indicators.rule: A U-shape: standards loosening a lot (-20) is a late-cycle sign (70), standards tightening hard (+50) means credit is already pulling back (95).
indicators.detail: Net share of banks reporting tighter standards on loans to large and mid-size businesses.

indicators.name: Investment-grade (BBB) corporate bond spread
indicators.rule: Heat is the higher of two rules: spreads historically tight (1.0 = 75, 1.6 = 40: priced for perfection) or widening fast (+0.3 in 60 days = 70). BBB is where many hyperscaler bonds sit.
indicators.detail: Extra yield investors demand for mid-grade corporate bonds. FRED carries about three years of this series.

indicators.name: SEC filings that pair GPUs with debt financing
indicators.display: 212 filing mentions in the last 90 days (1.5x the prior four 90-day periods, average 138)
indicators.rule: Heat 35 at the usual rate, 65 at 1.6x, 92 at 2.5x. Counts mentions in 8-Ks, prospectus supplements and shelf registrations that put GPUs next to credit agreements, notes, term loans, collateral or securitizations. A rising count means GPU purchases are increasingly debt-financed. Keyword matching is crude: some hits are incidental.
indicators.detail: Companies raising money against or for GPU purchases must say so in filings; this counts them.

indicators.name: Valuation (QQQ trailing P/E)
indicators.display: QQQ trailing P/E 26.4; price is 1.6% above its 200-day avg. Measures fragility, not timing: stretch showed no short-term crash edge in backt
indicators.detail: QQQ trailing P/E 26.4; price is 1.6% above its 200-day avg. Measures fragility, not timing: stretch showed no short-term crash edge in backtests.

indicators.name: Mega-cap concentration
indicators.display: Cap-weighted QQQ vs equal-weight QQQE: ratio moved -2.8% over 6 months.
indicators.rule: Change in cap-weighted vs equal-weighted QQQ over 6 months: +5 pts = 60, +15 pts = 90.
indicators.detail: Cap-weighted QQQ vs equal-weight QQQE: ratio moved -2.8% over 6 months.

indicators.name: Rates rising
indicators.rule: 10-year yield change over 3 months: +0.4 = 62, +1.0 = 92.
indicators.detail: 10Y yield 4.93%, +0.30 pts over 3 months.

indicators.name: Credit stress (junk bonds vs Treasuries)
indicators.display: High-yield bond fund is -2.3% vs Treasuries over 20 trading days. Falling = investors demanding more to hold risky debt.
indicators.rule: Junk bonds vs Treasuries over 20 days: -2% = 62, -6% = 95.
indicators.detail: High-yield bond fund is -2.3% vs Treasuries over 20 trading days. Falling = investors demanding more to hold risky debt.

indicators.name: Fear spike
indicators.display: VIX 19.4 is 1.21x its 50-day average. (Low VIX was NOT a useful warning in backtests.)
indicators.rule: Flashing if the VIX is above 1.25x its 50-day average (heat 75), else 20.
indicators.detail: VIX 19.4 is 1.21x its 50-day average. (Low VIX was NOT a useful warning in backtests.)

indicators.name: Trend breakdown
indicators.display: QQQ -9.1% from 1y high; below 50-day, above 200-day avg.
indicators.rule: Distance below the 1-year high: -7% = 62, -15% = 92.
indicators.detail: QQQ -9.1% from 1y high; below 50-day, above 200-day avg.

indicators.name: Semiconductor leadership break (AI narrative proxy)
indicators.display: SMH -3.2% over 10 days (-0.5 pts vs QQQ). Best-performing signal in backtests.
indicators.rule: Semiconductors vs the Nasdaq-100 over 10 days: lagging by 5 pts = 65, by 10 = 92. The best-performing signal in the original backtest.
indicators.detail: SMH -3.2% over 10 days (-0.5 pts vs QQQ). Best-performing signal in backtests.

indicators.name: Insider selling
indicators.display: NVDA/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META/AVGO insiders sold $1761M in 90 days vs $761M per-90d baseline (2.31x); bought $0.0M.
indicators.rule: Insider sales (six large AI names) vs their usual pace: 1.5x = 62, 3x = 92.
indicators.detail: NVDA/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META/AVGO insiders sold $1761M in 90 days vs $761M per-90d baseline (2.31x); bought $0.0M.

indicators.name: Stock market value vs the size of the economy
indicators.rule: Heat = where today's reading ranks among every day since 1988 (100 = the most extreme ever).
indicators.detail: Does the long record say this reading is unusual? Extreme readings preceded 2000 and 2008 but have also persisted for years.

indicators.name: Margin-loan growth
indicators.rule: Heat = where today's reading ranks among every day since 1985 (100 = the most extreme ever).
indicators.detail: Does the long record say this reading is unusual? Extreme readings preceded 2000 and 2008 but have also persisted for years.

indicators.name: Narrowing of market breadth (cap vs equal weight, 6 months)
indicators.rule: Heat = where today's reading ranks among every day since 2003 (100 = the most extreme ever).
indicators.detail: Does the long record say this reading is unusual? Extreme readings preceded 2000 and 2008 but have also persisted for years.

indicators.name: Two-year run-up of the Nasdaq-100
indicators.rule: Heat = where today's reading ranks among every day since 1987 (100 = the most extreme ever).
indicators.detail: Does the long record say this reading is unusual? Extreme readings preceded 2000 and 2008 but have also persisted for years.

indicators.name: Explosiveness of the price path (Phillips-Shi-Yu style test)
indicators.rule: Heat = where today's reading ranks among every day since 1986 (100 = the most extreme ever).
indicators.detail: Does the long record say this reading is unusual? Extreme readings preceded 2000 and 2008 but have also persisted for years.

indicators.name: Crash probability from the volatility model
indicators.display: 10.5% chance of a 15% fall in 60 trading days (typical 12.6%)
indicators.source: Prediction model v2 (owner page has the equation)
indicators.rule: Heat 35 at the typical probability, 65 at 20%, 90 at 30%. Well calibrated in 2003-17; no skill in the 2018-26 holdout, which is why this pillar has the smallest weight.
indicators.detail: Probability from market volatility alone. See the model page for what it can and cannot do.

indicators.name: Bubble-fragility index (21 indicators combined)
indicators.rule: Heat 35 at the typical level, 65 at 20%. Out-of-sample AUC 0.80 in 2003-17 and 0.50 in 2018-26 (chance), so it counts for half.
indicators.detail: The combined reading of valuation, margin debt, breadth, credit, rates and more.

indicators.name: VIX term structure (VIX divided by 3-month VIX)
indicators.display: 0.93 (above 1.00 = fear about the near term is higher than about next quarter)
indicators.rule: 0.90 = 25, 1.00 = 70 (the curve flips upside down), 1.10 = 95.
indicators.detail: Normally near-term fear is lower than long-term. When it inverts, traders are paying up for protection right now.

indicators.name: Bond-market volatility (MOVE index)
indicators.source: ICE BofA MOVE via Yahoo Finance
indicators.rule: Heat = where today's MOVE ranks among every day since 2002.
indicators.detail: Rates volatility spills into equity valuations, especially for long-duration growth stocks.

indicators.name: Tail-risk hedging demand (Cboe SKEW)
indicators.detail: A high SKEW means investors are paying extra for out-of-the-money puts: someone is positioned for a large fall even while the index rises.

indicators.name: Financial conditions (Chicago Fed NFCI)
indicators.rule: -0.4 = 20, -0.1 = 50, +0.3 = 85. Tightening is what usually ends a boom.
indicators.detail: 105 measures of risk, credit and leverage in one number.

indicators.name: Financial stress (St. Louis Fed index)
indicators.detail: 18 market series (yields, spreads, volatility) combined; zero is average stress.

indicators.name: Net liquidity (Fed assets minus reverse repo minus Treasury cash)
indicators.source: Federal Reserve and Treasury via FRED
indicators.detail: The cash actually sloshing through markets. Asset booms tend to need it growing.

indicators.name: Fed balance sheet, 13-week change
indicators.detail: Quantitative tightening drains reserves; easing adds them.

indicators.name: Real 10-year Treasury yield
indicators.detail: What safe money earns after inflation. High real yields shrink the present value of far-off profits, which is the whole case for AI stocks.

indicators.name: Market-implied inflation (5-year, 5 years forward)
indicators.detail: If investors stop trusting the Fed's inflation target, rates stay high and valuations compress.

indicators.name: Yield curve (10-year minus 3-month)
indicators.rule: Inverted = 65 and up; +0.5 = 35; +1.5 = 15. (Curves usually un-invert just before downturns.)
indicators.detail: An inverted curve has preceded every US recession since the 1960s, with a long and variable lag.

indicators.name: Corporate bond spread (Moody's Baa over 10-year Treasury)
indicators.rule: Heat = how TIGHT the spread is compared with every day since 1986 (tight = nothing priced for trouble).
indicators.detail: Booms end with spreads at their narrowest. Complacency is a fragility signal, not a trigger.

indicators.name: Junk-bond spread, 3-month widening
indicators.rule: Widening of 0.5 pt = 60, 1.5 pts = 92.
indicators.detail: The credit market usually stops believing before the stock market does.

indicators.name: Jobless claims vs their 1-year low (4-week average)
indicators.rule: 10% above the low = 25, 20% = 60, 35% = 92 (the Sahm-rule neighbourhood).
indicators.detail: Layoffs are the earliest hard evidence that demand is turning.

indicators.name: Consumer sentiment (Michigan)
indicators.detail: Weak households and strong stock prices is a gap that has historically closed from the stock side as often as the sentiment side.

indicators.name: 30-year mortgage rate
indicators.detail: Housing is the economy's most rate-sensitive sector and a major source of household wealth.

indicators.name: Broad US dollar, 3-month change
indicators.detail: A rising dollar tightens global financial conditions and squeezes companies that borrow in dollars.

indicators.name: Semiconductors vs the S&P 500, 3 months
indicators.rule: Chips lagging the market by 2 pts = 60, by 8 = 90. The AI trade leads on the way up and has led on the way down.
indicators.detail: If semiconductors stop outperforming, the AI narrative is losing its marginal buyer.

indicators.name: NVIDIA vs its own sector, 1 month
indicators.rule: NVIDIA lagging the semiconductor index by 3 pts = 60, 10 = 90.
indicators.detail: The bellwether tends to stumble before the sector.

indicators.name: TSMC (chip manufacturing): distance below 1-year high
indicators.rule: Within a few % of the high = 10; 8% below = 40; 15% = 70.
indicators.detail: Makes nearly every leading AI chip.

indicators.name: ASML (chip equipment): distance below 1-year high
indicators.rule: Within a few % of the high = 10; 8% below = 40; 15% = 70.
indicators.detail: Sells the machines that make the chips, so it sees orders first.

indicators.name: CoreWeave (GPU cloud, heavily indebted): distance below 1-year high
indicators.rule: Within a few % of the high = 10; 12% below = 40; 25% = 70.
indicators.detail: The most leveraged pure AI-infrastructure stock; it is the canary for the debt-funded part of the buildout.

indicators.name: How far the AI basket is stretched above its 200-day average
indicators.detail: Extension above long-run trend is the most dependable sign that expectations have run ahead of delivery, and the worst timer.

indicators.name: Speculative assets: how far below their highs (ARKK, Bitcoin)
indicators.display: average 12% below 1-year high; 100% of names below their 50-day average
indicators.rule: 60% weight: average distance below the 1-year high (8% = 40, 18% = 70, 30% = 95); 40% weight: share of names below their 50-day average (40% = 40, 70% = 75).
indicators.detail: Risk appetite shows up first in the most speculative corners.

indicators.name: US semiconductor production, year over year
indicators.rule: Heat = where this growth rate ranks since 1972 (booms in output are what overbuilding looks like from the inside).
indicators.detail: Real factory output: the physical side of the buildout.

indicators.name: AI infrastructure picks and shovels (power, cooling, servers, networking)
indicators.display: average 29% below 1-year high; 100% of names below their 50-day average
indicators.source: Yahoo Finance (VRT, ETN, DELL, SMCI, ANET)
indicators.rule: 60% weight: average distance below the 1-year high (8% = 40, 18% = 70, 30% = 95); 40% weight: share of names below their 50-day average (40% = 40, 70% = 75).
indicators.detail: These are the companies selling into data-center construction; they roll over when orders slow.

indicators.name: Reader interest in the 'AI bubble' Wikipedia article
indicators.display: 4767 views a day this week, 2.7x the prior three months
indicators.rule: Same as usual = 30, double = 65, quadruple = 92.
indicators.detail: Public attention to the bubble question. Spikes often follow sell-offs, and the first big spike has often marked late-stage booms.

indicators.name: Headline tone on AI stocks (last 3 days)
indicators.display: 20 of 26 tagged headlines lean negative (20 negative, 6 positive)
indicators.source: Google News headlines, simple word list
indicators.rule: A crude word-list score. 40% negative = 35, 60% = 65, 80% = 90.
indicators.detail: Rough and noisy. It records the mood of the coverage, not whether it is right.
